29 The double-slit experiment demonstrates interference between two coherent sources of light
waves. In the diagram, the curved lines represent wavefronts.
At which point does complete destructive interference (a minimum) occur?
A
C
B
D
single slit
double slit

hints: Look at the curved lines to the right of the double slit and notice that each line is a crest, so the gap halfway between two adjacent lines is a trough.
Recall that complete destructive interference needs antiphase superposition, where path difference $= (n + \frac{1}{2})\lambda$ and a crest from one slit meets a trough from the other slit.
Compare point B where two crests cross on the central line with point C where a crest from one slit falls in the gap between crests from the other slit.
walkthrough: The single slit spreads one wave to illuminate both slits in phase, so the upper and lower slits act as two coherent sources whose circular wavefronts overlap to the right.
The curved lines show positions of crests. Constructive interference occurs where crest meets crest, and complete destructive interference occurs where crest meets trough.
At B on the central axis the distances from the two slits are equal, so the path difference is $0$. The two sets of crests arrive together, giving a maximum.
At D the two sets of curved crests again cross each other crest-on-crest, so the waves are in phase and reinforce.
At C the crest from one slit arrives where the other wave is halfway between crests, i.e. at a trough. The path difference is half a wavelength, so the displacements cancel to give a minimum.
Cancellation of equal-amplitude crest and trough gives complete destructive interference. This is option C.

A.explanation: Point A is to the left of the double slit where only the single-slit wave exists, so there are not two overlapping waves to cancel.

B.explanation: At B a curved wavefront from the upper slit crosses a curved wavefront from the lower slit, so crest meets crest for constructive interference.

C.explanation: At C a wavefront from one slit falls midway between two wavefronts from the other slit, so crest meets trough for complete destructive interference.

D.explanation: At D curved wavefronts from the two slits again intersect crest-on-crest, giving constructive interference, not a minimum.
